faq.description: Have another question? Open an issue on GitHub or reach out by email.

items.question: What is HighClaw?
items.answer: HighClaw is a high-performance AI Agent infrastructure written in Go. It provides multi-agent collaboration, distributed architecture, and integrations with 12+ messaging platforms and 22+ AI providers — all compiled into a single binary.

items.question: How is HighClaw different from OpenClaw?
items.answer: HighClaw is written in Go instead of Python, delivering significantly better performance and lower resource usage. It features a single binary deployment model, native distributed multi-agent support, and a hybrid memory system combining vector search, full-text search, and knowledge graphs.

items.question: What platforms does HighClaw support?
items.answer: HighClaw integrates with 12+ messaging platforms including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, DingTalk, Lark, WhatsApp, and LINE. It also supports 22+ AI providers including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Ollama.

items.question: How do I deploy HighClaw?
items.answer: HighClaw compiles to a single Go binary. You can deploy it with `go build && ./highclaw`, use the provided Docker image, or deploy to any cloud platform. No runtime dependencies required.

items.question: Can I run multiple agents?
items.answer: Yes! HighClaw's distributed multi-agent architecture supports running 100+ specialized agents with A2A communication, sub-task delegation, and collaborative problem solving — with zero performance degradation.

items.question: Is HighClaw open source?
items.answer: Yes. HighClaw is 100% open source under the MIT License. You can deploy it on your own infrastructure, customize it freely, and contribute to the project on GitHub.
